text: The propositions separating computative from neoclassical labor markets are concrete hypotheses with neoclassical nulls — on allocation efficiency, participation formation under standing-based entry, cooperation stability under defection incentives, and capture resistance — each evaluable in controlled multi-agent settings now.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, From Neoclassical to Computative Labor: Foundations for a Testable Theory of Reputation Governance in the Agent Economy (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6890879

isBasedOn.name: From Neoclassical to Computative Labor: Foundations for a Testable Theory of Reputation Governance in the Agent Economy

abstract: Each of these is a hypothesis with a neoclassical null, and each can be evaluated in controlled multi-agent settings without waiting for a mature agent economy to arrive.
